craft_notes: Sthāyin: raudra of grinding; vyabhicāri raudra-utsāha at doubt-split-fine. Sanskrit-first: niyamana-niṣedha pair per UNC (RULE-THEN-BAN — kept pair, both verbs); Yama emitted (sṛṣṭvā — made, kept made); piṃṣ (GRIND — kept grinding, fine). Rows: 9 (rule/ban/show/grind — four acts of world-stilling), 1 (‘fine’ closes — fineness last: doubt ground fine). Close: ‘grind my world-fear fine’. Rupture: em-dash (stilled stated, then its method — loosing it, then ruling it). Rejected: ‘forbid’ for ban — killed: ban bans; ‘crush’ for grind — killed: grind grinds fine (fineness IS the point). Read aloud: TO-still THE-world BY-loos-ing-IT — RULE of-DOUBT-fear, THEN-ban — … SPLIT-doubt a-GAIN, GREAT-god-DESS, GRIND my-WORLD-fear FINE.

lines: To still the world by loosing it — rule of doubt-fear, then ban —
You show, having made Yama. Split doubt again, great goddess, grind my world-fear fine.
